constrained-survivability.description: Can the system operate at all under resource budget? Measures operational correctness, not performance.
constrained-survivability.primary_question: Does the system remain alive, non-crashing, and minimally correct under the declared budget?
constrained-survivability.comparison_policy: cross-target comparison only allowed after cgroup accounting verified and artifact_provenance fields populated. JVM vs native-image comparisons require separate cgroup limit per artifact_kind.

efficiency-density.description: What useful work per unit of constrained resource? Requires validated effective_cpu and heap accounting.
efficiency-density.primary_question: How much successful work does the system deliver per unit of CPU and memory budget?
efficiency-density.comparison_policy: Cross-target comparison forbidden until cpu_throttle_ratio is captured and effective_vcpu = declared_vcpu * (1 - cpu_throttle_ratio) is validated. JVM overlay flags must not be applied to native-image targets.
efficiency-density.denominator_note: effective_vcpu = declared_vcpu * (1 - cpu_throttle_ratio). Current constrained-smoke data shows ~94% throttle rate (585/623 periods for JVM Quarkus track-c). Efficiency claims require at least guard-class runs with stable throttle ratio across multiple runs.

performance-ceiling.description: Maximum throughput with headroom. Entirely separate from constrained families. Requires separate scenarios and unconstrained execution profiles.
performance-ceiling.primary_question: What is the maximum sustainable throughput with full resource access?
performance-ceiling.comparison_policy: Must not be compared to constrained-survivability or efficiency-density results. Separate scenario, separate contract, separate result namespace.

smoke.note: Confirms system starts and responds. Not suitable for stability or efficiency claims. All current constrained results are at this level.

guard.note: Minimum for resource trend detection. Required before efficiency-density metrics are considered non-trivial.

regression.note: Required for regression tracking and stability assertions.

contract.note: Required for 1.0 efficiency_contract validation. Includes restart-under-constraint evidence.

correctness_under_constraint.description: Axis 1. Is the system correct under budget? Covers error rate, timeout rate, crash/OOM detection.
correctness_under_constraint.note: Smoke-level sufficient for boolean survivability. Guard required for trend interpretation.

cost_efficiency.description: Axis 2. Successful work per unit resource. Requires throttle ratio and heap accounting.
cost_efficiency.note: Smoke-level data is insufficient for efficiency claims. Throttle ratio must be stable across at least 2 runs before computing efficiency-density metrics.

degradation_behavior.description: Axis 3. How does the system degrade as load increases beyond budget? Requires load-ramp scenario, not single-point.
degradation_behavior.note: Requires sweep scenario (load ramp under fixed budget), not a fixed-rate single-point run. Current entity-read-by-id smoke runs are insufficient for degradation behavior claims.

stability.description: Axis 4. Does the system remain stable over extended constrained operation? Detects leaks, GC pressure, thread accumulation.
stability.note: 30s smoke has no stability signal. 10m guard provides trend. 30m regression is minimum for stability assertion. 2h contract required for 1.0 efficiency contract claim.

efficiency_contract_v1.description: Efficiency contract for Exeris 1.0 under constrained budget. Defines survivability and efficiency floors, not performance ceilings.

constraints.no_crash_under_budget: System must not OOM-kill, crash, or fail to restart within the declared cgroup memory and CPU budget across the full contract soak duration.
constraints.degradation_monotonicity: Under increasing load within budget, degradation must be monotonic: latency increases before error rate increases, error rate increases before crash. Non-monotonic degradation (sudden crash without prior latency/error signal) is a contract violation.
constraints.degradation_observability: The transition from healthy to degraded must be observable via metrics no later than 2 measurement intervals before service becomes unavailable. Silent failure is a contract violation.
